solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former copper's competent and easily forgiven

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, so EX means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive
able means competent

explanation.surface: A retired policeman is capable and readily pardoned for his lapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but here it is the metal, chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something excusable can be pardoned without much difficulty, which is what being easily forgiven means.

clue.text: Some characters of greater interest for poetic Ireland

indicators.note: some characters of means a run of letters is taken from within these words

explanation.surface: Some features of more intriguing poems about Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is the old literary and poetic name for Ireland, from the Irish Éirinn.

clue.text: Exclusive group with somewhere to sleep north of lake

indicators.note: in a down clue north of puts the bed word above the lake

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A select set with a bed above a lake, like a holiday lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small, select circle of people with shared interests, an exclusive group.

clue.text: Flag celebrated with any number coming out

indicators.note: coming out means the number letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to sing someone's praises is to celebrate them, so sang means celebrated
n is the mathematical symbol for any number

explanation.surface: A flag is honoured as various numbers emerge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but here it is the verb meaning to droop.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or droop, and to sag is to droop or weaken in the same way.

clue.text: Desolate pub gets torn apart, almost

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, to tear apart

explanation.surface: A bleak bar is nearly ripped to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land is bleak and lifeless, which is a synonym for desolate.

clue.text: English person of wisdom outside very good on secret assignments?

indicators.note: outside means the wise person word wraps around the following pieces

parts.note: a sage is a wise person
pi is a crossword abbreviation of pious, very good

explanation.surface: An English wise man engaged in clandestine work.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that secret assignments only describes spying by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage is spying, and secret assignments are the missions spies carry out, so it is a loose descriptive definition.

clue.text: Idiot presents ring to a female

parts.note: the letter O is ring-shaped
F is the standard abbreviation for female; the run of letters across to a female is a coincidence, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A fool hands a ring over to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, stupid person, a straightforward synonym for an idiot.

clue.text: Month ending with out-of-this world group performing

indicators.note: ending with means the month is finished off by the alien letters

parts.note: Oct is short for October
ET is the extraterrestrial of the film, someone from out of this world

explanation.surface: A month that closes with an otherworldly band on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight musicians who play together.

clue.text: Raider for ever right

parts.note: taken as written
aye is a poetic and Scots word for always or ever

explanation.surface: A plunderer whose motto might be 'for ever right'.
explanation.definitionFit: A forayer makes forays, sudden attacks into enemy territory, so is a raider.

clue.text: Number, for example, in Bury

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'for example' is placed in the word for bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Something numerical happening, say, in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also a town in Lancashire, England, which is the surface reading; here it is the verb meaning inter.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, so the answer is a kind of number.

clue.text: The old man, artist losing home

indicators.note: losing means the letters for home are dropped from the word for artist

parts.note: a painter is an artist
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A father who paints has lost his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is Latin for father, and 'the old man' is informal British slang for one's father.

clue.text: Whinger to cry, frightfully embarrassing

indicators.note: frightfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A moaner bursting into tears is painfully awkward to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightfully' seems to intensify 'embarrassing' but is the anagram signal; a whinger is a British word for a complainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cringeworthy makes you squirm with awkwardness, which is to say it is embarrassing.

clue.text: Most restricted home gets object tipped inside

indicators.note: inside means the tipped object goes within the home word

parts.note: a bird's nest is its home
an arrow is an object with a pointed tip

explanation.surface: A cramped house where something has been knocked over indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped' suggests knocked over but means having a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowest is the superlative of narrow, meaning most limited or confined.

clue.text: Quiet attempt to encapsulate Old English verse

indicators.note: to encapsulate means quiet plus attempt wrap around the abbreviation for Old English

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken effort to summarise Anglo-Saxon poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is writing in metrical lines, which is another word for poetry.

clue.text: People initially inclined to be flexible

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word that comes before it

parts.note: liable to do something means inclined to do it

explanation.surface: People tend at first to be accommodating.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliable means easily bent or persuaded, a synonym of flexible.

clue.text: Town to prohibit travel before end of war

indicators.note: before places the travel word ahead of the final letter

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
to go is to travel

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of war

explanation.surface: A town moves to forbid journeys until the fighting is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangor is a town in north Wales (there is another in Northern Ireland).
explanation.definitionFit: Bangor is a cathedral city and town in Wales, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Acquire maiden maybe and become better after

parts.note: to get is to acquire
in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, so it is an example of an over

explanation.surface: Win over a young woman and then feel better.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket over is a set of six balls; a maiden over is one where no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To get over an illness or setback is to recover from it, becoming better after it.

clue.text: The Spanish moan, upset and weak

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
beef is slang for a complaint or moan

explanation.surface: The Spaniard grumbles, distressed and frail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as distressed but turns EL BEEF backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble means lacking strength, which is a direct synonym of weak.

clue.text: ''Invest more somehow'' — politician involved in reforms

indicators.note: involved in means the politician is placed inside the rearranged letters
somehow implies the letters of the quoted phrase are put together in some other way

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A politician urging more investment as part of a reform programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal shuffles INVEST MORE, and involved in puts MP inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Reforms are changes made to make things better, which is what improvements are.

clue.text: Walk around bottom of village for serenity

indicators.note: around means the walk word goes round the letter taken from village

parts.note: to pace is to walk

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Strolling round the lower end of a village brings calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace is a state of calm and tranquillity, which serenity also describes.

clue.text: Good boy is happy

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A well-behaved boy is content.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad means pleased or cheerful, a common synonym for happy.

clue.text: Daring Bishop facing rant

indicators.note: facing puts the bishop letter in front of the rant word

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to rave is to rant

explanation.surface: A bold bishop confronting a tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and daring both describe someone willing to face danger, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Torment where sick person is confined — not good

parts.note: an ill person is confined to bed
evil is the opposite of good

explanation.surface: The suffering of being bedridden is a bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to plague or harass persistently, which is to torment.

clue.text: Insult can be hell

definitions.meaning: slang for to insult or disrespect someone
The Roman god of the underworld and, by extension, the underworld itself, as in Dante

explanation.surface: An insult can be a hellish thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dis is both a slang verb for disrespecting and the classical name for the infernal underworld.

clue.text: Unknown character reported in Devon river

indicators.note: reported means the letter is spoken rather than written, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: x is the classic unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure is said to be in a river in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the Exe flows through Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exe is a river rising on Exmoor and flowing through the county of Devon to the sea.

clue.text: True dears, awfully precious

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of these words are put together badly, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: Loyal loved ones are terribly dear to us.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is held dear and valued highly, which is what precious means.
